cost: sha/time formatting O(input bytes)/O(1) arithmetic respectively; glob O(visited directory entries plus sort) with star matching substring scans. Memory proportional to candidates and returned paths; filesystem effects are reads.
description: Time, card labels and simple filesystem glob
forward: sha1_hex returns lowercase digest; ts decomposes seconds using Euclidean day/rem and Gregorian civil conversion. date_suffix takes final ten bytes and tests digit/dash shape. expand handles only ~ and ~/; glob walks components, star-matches directory names, suppresses unreadable directories, retains files and sorts. wild matches prefix, sequential interior fragments and suffix.
inverse: Nonmatching glob names cannot enter the next component frontier, and directories cannot remain final outputs. Invalid date shape yields None on safe slicing domain; impossible calendar dates are not excluded.

A timestamp's compatible seconds are unique within the civil conversion's valid domain, while a date suffix result admits arbitrary prefixes. Sorted glob output does not reconstruct directory iteration order or ignored read errors; SHA1 is many-to-one.
secs=-1 decomposes into days=-1, rem=86399, avoiding negative time fields. ts uses proleptic Gregorian cycles; now_ts maps preepoch clock error to zero.
wild splits only star; leading fragment must be prefix, interior fragments found in order consuming their bytes, final fragment suffix. Question mark and brackets are literal, not shell syntax.
English and escaped legacy labels map to shared English keys; card_part normalizes only the two declared totals and preserves other labels.
parent_name/stem/file_name use lossy UTF-8; abs canonicalizes with an error on missing paths. expand leaves ~other unchanged; filesystem permissions and races remain external.
limitations: Finite helper/fixture evidence only; no DuckDB integration or SQL semantics

state: glob output sorted lexicographically, files only; paths need not be canonical. date_suffix is not calendar validation and slicing requires a UTF-8 boundary at len-10. Timestamp computation on i64 seconds has bounded day arithmetic but display years may exceed four digits.
